frequency_question: What proportion of major federal bills complete all mandatory Senate procedural steps (committee review, floor placement, debate, and final roll call vote) within a 271-day operating calendar window?
membership_rule: Includes all bills introduced in the Senate or received from the House that underwent committee referral and reached a final floor vote in the Senate within any 271-day timeframe of a congressional session. Excludes fast-track reconciliation bills or emergency suspensions of rules.
coverage_note: 6 representative major federal bills sampled; estimated roughly 40 similar major non-budget bills in total across the timeframe.
known_gaps: Excludes minor technical amendments and unanimous consent packages.
skeleton: Legislative days available in a 271-day calendar window (~75 floor days) divided by average cumulative procedural timeline for non-reconciliation bills.
multiplier: 6 months nominal processing time for standard committee and floor scheduling steps within a 9-month window.
validity_reason: Senate standing rules and procedural timelines remain stable across multiple Congresses unless the filibuster is fundamentally altered.
